Definition: of Hebrew origin (H3667); Chanaan (i.e. Kenaan), the early name of Palestine:--Chanaan.
BiblicalUsage: Chanaan is the Greek spelling of Canaan, the early name of the land of Palestine, and it appears in Stephen's defence and in Paul's sermon. Stephen tells how a famine came over all the land of Egypt and Chanaan, and Paul, preaching at Pisidian Antioch, tells how God destroyed seven nations in the land of Chanaan and divided their land to Israel by lot.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the name matters because both speeches are histories: Stephen and Paul each retell the same story of a land promised, taken, and given. The Greek spelling is only a doorway into the Hebrew Canaan, and the land itself is the thread that runs through both sermons.
RelatedEvents: Martyrdom of Stephen; Paul Preaches at Pisidian Antioch
